Title: Quick Play Guide
Event: Congratulations! You are hired as the project manager. In this row you will learn the relevant part of the story of the particular space.
Action: This row will summarise the actions that may need to be done to progress the game.
Outcome: And this row is items chosen by chance… but not always because you can reject lady luck and NEGOTIATE.
w_card: The scope of work is W cards. Here you learn how to add remove or change scope. Just remember 20% design fee is the max.
b_card: You can not build if you do not have $ - Bank will lend you a little $ rather quickly and at a low rate.
i_card: You can not build if you do not have $ - Investor will lend you a lot of $ rather slowly and at a higher rate.
l_card: In real life shit happens all the time. In this game it only happens here.
e_card: Once in a while you may want specialized help. It is available in this row. But will it help you or hinder you.
Time: Time is $ and time is always ticking here. So keep your eye out on this space.
Fee: Of course to get things unstuck or get things done at all - you have to pay people up front. Watch this trickle so it does not become a flood.
space_1: Lastly you may have choices of where to go next.
space_2: These are alternative paths available to you.
space_3: Some spaces offer 3-5 different next destinations.
space_4: Choose wisely as each path affects your strategy.
space_5: Some spaces require special conditions to unlock paths.
Negotiate: and if you really really really do not like your choices... Sometimes you can refuse them and just try again.

Title: Strategy Guide
Event: Now that you read the first column and know the rules - here is your strategy guide:
Action: You just got hired by an owner. The 2 of you will dream up / design / review and build a project.
Outcome: Strategise and pick the right dice rolls
w_card: while being aware of the 20% design fee limit.
b_card: Watch out how much you borrow
i_card: and from whom. Bank offers quick small loans at low rates.
l_card: Beware that in the meantime life happens
e_card: so don't forget to use your Expeditor help. Investor offers large loans at higher rates but takes longer.
Time: and try to do it as quickly as possible.
Fee: Pay attention to fees - they accumulate quickly
space_1: and choose the most advantageous path to win.
space_2: Each space offers different movement options.
space_3: Plan your route based on your current resources.
space_4: Some paths are faster but riskier.
space_5: Others are safer but take more time.
Negotiate: Don't forget waiting 1 extra turn if the roll is really bad may be more advantageous.

Title: The owner walks you through it
Event: Sit down. I've been turning this project over for months — let me walk you through what I want built. You're going to hear it from me first, before anyone else gets a say.
Action: Lock the scope as offered, or push back and revisit tomorrow.
e_card_narrative: I'm handing you a stack of contacts — expeditors I've worked with before. Take all three; you'll need every one of them before this project is done.

Title: The owner opens the books
Event: Here's what I'm putting in — {fundingAmount}. Look it over. I'm not negotiating against myself — but if you've got a real reason to push back, I'll hear it.
Action: Take the check, or push for more and revisit tomorrow.
Outcome: Owner's funding is in. Starting budget is set.

Title: I pick a direction
Event: I'm picking a direction. Expeditor and I have talked it through, but the call's mine. Time to commit.
Action: Trim the team, see how the days shake out, commit to a path.
Outcome: Direction set. Tomorrow I move on it.

Title: I rethink the plan
Event: Rethinking the plan. Life's moving fast, my staff's restless, and the first try didn't pan out.
Action: A staff member quits for a better gig. Days pass. Commit to a new plan.
Outcome: New direction locked. Time to act.
e_card: The person to your right takes a card.

Title: I'm flipping through your plan
Event: Sit down. I've got your plan in front of me — let's see if it holds up. I'll cut you a rate, but I want my pound of flesh on the scope first.
Action: Negotiate scope and rate. Lock in the terms, or push for better.
Outcome: Terms agreed. On to the bank.

Title: You again. Already.
Event: You're back. Cash didn't last? Sit down — I'll listen, but the warmth's gone. This round it's whatever I'm willing to put up. You take it.
Action: Re-pitch the ask. Take whatever the lender offers this time.

Title: We're underwriting your file
Event: We've got your file. Underwriting will work the numbers — amount, rate, timeline. We'll come back with terms. Standard process. Sit tight.
Action: Sign the loan terms, or push for a lower rate.
Outcome: Loan approved at the bank's terms. Money incoming.
Fee: 1% for loan of up to $1.4M or 2% for loan between $1.5M and 2.75M or 3% above 2.75M

Title: We see you're back
Event: You're back with us. We've already underwritten this project once for {fundingAmount} — second pass means a closer look and a tighter rate. Patience is shorter on this side too.
Action: A banker stops returning your calls. Take the revised loan, whatever it looks like.
Outcome: New terms in hand. Whatever they are.
Fee: 1% for loan of up to $1.4M or 2% for loan between $1.5M and 2.75M or 3% above 2.75M

Title: The committee will hear you out
Event: The committee will hear you out. We're slower than the bank and we cost more — but we move real money when we like the deal. Walk us through it.
Action: Sign with the investors, or push for better terms.

Title: The committee's seen you before
Event: You're back. We've already put real money into this project once ({fundingAmount}) — the appetite for sweetening terms is gone. Take what we offer this round, or come back later.
Action: An investor contact gets pulled into another deal. Take whatever terms come back.
Outcome: Took what the committee offered. Moving on.
e_card: The person to your left takes a card.

Title: Hunting for an architect
Event: I'm hunting for an architect. Calls, resumes, interviews — it takes days. I'd rather be building.
Action: Work the phones. See who turns up.
review_loop_message: Design changes are needed. You must consult with the architect to revise the plans before resubmitting.

Title: I want another look at these drawings
Event: I've been thinking about these drawings overnight and something's off. Give me another pass — I think we can do better. Push back if you have to, but I'd rather get this right than fast.
Action: Accept the redesign, or push back on the changes.
review_loop_message: Design changes are needed. You must consult with the architect to revise the plans before resubmitting.

Title: Let's talk about my fee
Event: We need to talk money. I've put real time into this — sketches, options, conversations with the consultants. The fee covers the work I've already done. It's not unreasonable.
Action: Cut a contact to save budget. Pay the fee, or push back.
Outcome: Fee agreed. Moving to the design work.
l_card_narrative: You've been on this job a while — sometimes things just happen. Keep your head down and hope today isn't one of those days.
e_card_narrative: You're cutting staff to save budget. One of your expeditors has to go — pick carefully, they're hard to replace.

Title: There's more to the work than I quoted
Event: The scope grew. It always does. The original fee covered the original drawings — what's been added needs to be paid for separately. I'm not nickel-and-diming. This is the actual extra work.
Action: Pay the extra, or push back on the upcharge.
l_card_narrative: Back again, and life doesn't stop throwing curveballs. Roll the dice and see what lands.
e_card_narrative: Your architect friend recommends someone new. Add them to your roster — you'll need the help later.

Title: Today is the design reveal
Event: Today's the day. We've finished the design — every elevation, every section, every detail. Sit through the presentation, then we'll talk about whether it's ready for engineering.
Action: Watch the presentation. Sign off on the design, or send it back.

Title: Here's the revised design
Event: Took your feedback. Here are the revised drawings — I think you'll see the changes. If they don't land, send it back again, but I'd rather we converge this round.
Action: Compare the new drawings to the old. Sign off on the revisions, or send them back again.
e_card: The person to your right takes a card.

Title: Hunting for an engineer
Event: I'm hunting for a structural engineer. Same grind as the architect — calls, credentials, interviews.
Action: Work the phones. See who turns up.
review_loop_message: Structural or engineering modifications required. The engineer needs to update calculations or drawings.

Title: I need another pass at the calcs
Event: I've been over the structural calculations and I want another pass. Numbers don't lie — if something's off, we fix it now, before steel orders or pour schedules. I'd rather slow down here than have it back at me later.
Action: Accept the engineer's findings, or ask for another pass.
review_loop_message: Structural or engineering modifications required. The engineer needs to update calculations or drawings.

Title: Let's settle the fee
Event: Let's settle the fee. Structural is precise work — load calcs, code review, stamped drawings. The number reflects the liability I carry on this. I don't pad it.
Action: Every penny counts. Pay the fee, or push back.
Outcome: Fee settled. On to the design.

Title: More work, more fee
Event: Scope grew. Load calcs need redoing. Either you pay for the additional engineering, or we sign off on what's already there — and I don't recommend that.
Action: Pay the extra, or push back on the upcharge.

Title: Structural design is done
Event: Structural design is done. I know it took a while — that's what conservative load paths and code review get you. Sit through the presentation. The numbers are sound.
Action: Watch the presentation. Sign off on the structure, or send it back.
Outcome: Structural design signed off. Filings next.

Title: Revised structure, same standards
Event: Revised drawings. The changes are subtle — that's how structural revisions work. I'm not redesigning the wheel, I'm tightening the calcs. Compare them properly before you tell me they look the same.
Action: Compare the new drawings to the old. Accept the revised structure, or send it back again.

Title: I'm not signing off until you hear me
Event: This one's not yours to call alone. There are pieces of this project I won't budge on — let me tell you which way it's going. You can argue if you want, but you'll lose.
Action: Hear the owner out. Go with the owner's call, or push back.
Outcome: The owner's call is locked in.

Title: I want to see the finish line
Event: Enough back and forth. I want to see this thing finished — here's my call. Take it and move, or come back tomorrow with a better argument.
Action: Owner's decided fast this round. Go with it, or push for one more round.

Title: I cut a corner
Event: Owner said get this done at any cost. I'm going to cut a corner. Odds aren't in my favor — I know it.
Action: Quietly let a contact go for deniability. See if the move lands.
Outcome: I made my move. Now we see if it stuck.

Title: Careful version
Event: Last time didn't go well. I'm being a lot more careful this time.
Action: Quietly part ways with another contact. See how the careful version lands.

Title: Department of Buildings counter
Event: Department of Buildings. You're here to pay the filing fee — 1% of project value. Standard rate. Sign here, here, and here. We don't haggle on this.
Action: Pay the fee. Hire a few hands to keep the filing clean.
Outcome: Fees paid. You're in the system.

Title: DOB add-on bill
Event: You're back. Add-on fees are owed — review the bill and pay. Once you've paid the original, the add-ons aren't up for debate. We've already done the work on this file.
Action: Swap a worn-out helper. Pay the extra.

Title: I pick my DOB route
Event: I'm picking my filing path. Plan Exam is slow but safe. Prof Cert is fast but risky. The owner wants this done — so do I. The call's mine.
Action: Plan Exam is slower but safer. Prof Cert is faster but riskier. Pick.
Outcome: Path chosen. I live with it.

Title: Waiting in the DOB line
Event: Clerks are slow today. Nothing to do but wait — paperwork moves at the line's pace, not mine.
Action: Hurry up and wait. That's the DOB rhythm.

Title: I'm reading your plans
Event: I'm working through your plans page by page — every elevation, every section. Checking against code. Nothing personal. If there's an objection, I'll write it up. Save us both time and submit clean.
Action: Accept the examiner's verdict, or resubmit with revisions.
review_loop_message: The examiner found minor issues that need to be addressed. Additional documentation or corrections are required before continuing.

Title: I'm reading the resubmission
Event: I'm reading the resubmission. I flip faster on the second pass — I already know what to look for. If you fixed the objections, it'll go quick. If you didn't, it'll go quicker.
Action: Accept the second read, or resubmit again.
review_loop_message: The examiner found minor issues that need to be addressed. Additional documentation or corrections are required before continuing.

Title: Prof Cert filing accepted
Event: Prof Cert filing. Self-certified — we barely look. That's the deal you signed up for. Stamp it, file it, you're out the door. Just hope the data entry hand types your numbers right — that's on you, not us.
Action: File and hope no one checks too hard.

Title: You again — second cert
Event: You again. Hand it over. Hope your expeditor filled the forms right — at this counter, errors aren't our problem. They're yours.
Action: File and hope.

Title: Auditor's at your file
Event: I've pulled your file. ZR-23.5, ZR-25-13, that side yard variance you skipped — I cite them from memory because that's my job. Audits aren't paranoid. They're routine. The findings are yours to accept or contest.
Action: Read the findings. Accept them, or dispute.

Title: Down to the last objections
Event: You've cleared most of the objections. A few remain. We'll close them out one of two ways — you accept the final findings, or we have one more conversation. I'd recommend the first.
Action: Down to the last few. Accept the final call, or push the last few.

Title: FDNY intake desk
Event: FDNY intake. We deal with what kills people in fires — sprinklers, standpipes, alarms, egress. Don't dance with us. Yes/no questions, straight answers. You hedge, we catch it.
Action: Answer the routing questions. Be straight — they catch a hedge.
space_1: Did you pass FDNY approval before? YES - Space 2 - NO - Space 3
space_2: Did the scope change since the last visit? YES - REG-FDNY-PLAN-EXAM - NO - Space 3
space_3: Did Department of Buildings send you here? YES - REG-FDNY-PLAN-EXAM - NO - Space 4
space_4: Do you have: sprinklers / standpipe / fire alarm / fire suppression? YES - REG-FDNY-PLAN-EXAM - NO - Space 5
space_5: Do you have  DOB approval? YES - PM-DECISION-CHECK or CON-INITIATION NO - REG-DOB-TYPE-SELECT

Title: FDNY intake, second visit
Event: Second visit. We remember faces here. Recognition usually means more attention, not less. Same questions — answer them the same way.
Action: Run through intake again. Be straight — they remember inconsistencies.
space_1: Did you pass FDNY approval before? YES - Space 2 - NO - Space 3
space_2: Did the scope change since the last visit? YES - REG-FDNY-PLAN-EXAM - NO - Space 3
space_3: Did Department of Buildings send you here? YES - REG-FDNY-PLAN-EXAM - NO - Space 4
space_4: Do you have: sprinklers / standpipe / fire alarm / fire suppression? YES - REG-FDNY-PLAN-EXAM - NO - Space 5
space_5: Do you have  DOB approval? YES - PM-DECISION-CHECK or CON-INITIATION NO - REG-DOB-TYPE-SELECT

Title: FDNY plan exam
Event: I read for what kills people in fires. Sprinkler heads, standpipe risers, egress widths, alarm zones. Sound like you know the code if you want — I actually know it. Objections come back specific.
Action: Accept FDNY's verdict, or push back on objections.
review_loop_message: Fire safety review identified items needing attention. The FDNY examiner requires additional information or modifications.

Title: FDNY second read — final
Event: You've been here once. We don't do third negotiations — this round you get a stamp or you don't. Sit quietly. Speak only when spoken to.
Action: Approval stamp or denial stamp — which one comes out?
review_loop_message: Fire safety review identified items needing attention. The FDNY examiner requires additional information or modifications.

Title: Sit down, let's talk price
Event: Sit down. You need someone to build this thing — I'm your guy. Quality, cost, schedule — pick two, but I'll be straight with you on all three. Cheap crew costs you on the back end. Good crew costs you up front. Your call.
Action: Quality and cost multiplier on the table. Sign the contractor, or push back on the price.

Title: Change order on the table
Event: Look — things shifted on site. Found something we couldn't see in the drawings. I need a change order. Time extension, extra fee. Not unreasonable. But it's not free either.
Action: Sign the change order, or push back.
try_again_label: Push back on the change order

Title: We hit something in the field
Event: Boss — we hit something in the field. Wasn't on the drawings. Every hour we're stopped costs you. Need to swap a body in for the right specialist. We can fix it on site if we move now.
Action: Swap a contact for the right specialist. Try to fix it on site.

Title: Another one in the field
Event: Boss — another one. Construction sites don't hand you problems one at a time, they pile up. Every day we're slowed costs you. Push hard or eat the delay.
Action: Push hard to head off the delay. No time to spare.
e_card: The person to your right takes a card.

Title: Inspector just walked in
Event: Boss — inspector just walked onto the site. Looks fresh, that cuts both ways. There's a safety violation by the southwest corner — let me steer them somewhere else while you handle the paperwork.
Action: Steer their attention elsewhere. See if it works.

Title: Johnes is back for the follow-up
Event: Boss — Inspector Johnes is back. He never liked you, but he's fair. Frank's crew just wrapped, two of his guys can join us for the walk. Extra eyes, extra hands. Keep our story straight.
Action: Walk the site with the inspector. Steady answers, no volunteered info.

Title: Final review counter
Event: Final review. Birthday party in the back office — everything's running an hour late. You picked a good day to come in. Maybe your file gets a softer read. Maybe.
Action: Accept the verdict, or ask for another pass.

Title: Final review, second pass
Event: Bad day at the counter. Supervisor's consoling a clerk who just got chewed out. Files are crawling. Hope nobody notices the photocopy where the original should be.
Action: Accept the verdict, or ask for another pass.

Title: You delivered
Event: You delivered. Took longer than I wanted, cost more than I budgeted — but it's done, and it's done right. That's what matters in the end. Good work.
Action: Final score gets calculated here.

Title: Project Complete!
Event: You Completed project!
Action: YOU ARE done! Calculate final score.
Outcome: Project's already delivered. Final score's locked in.
